caption: A person carrying a stack of dinner plates in one hand trips on a rug, and the plates slide off and shatter on the floor.

sa.check: A person carries a stack of dinner plates in one hand.
The person trips on a rug.
The plates slide off the hand.
The rug is where the trip happens.
The trip comes first, then the slide, then the shattering.

pc.expect: The plates leave the hand as the person stumbles and fall to the floor.
pc.fail: The plates hang in the air; or they rise; or they stay on the hand while the person falls.

pc.expect: The plates break on impact and the pieces scatter; they do not break in the air or bounce whole.
pc.fail: They break in mid-air; or bounce off the floor whole; or flatten like dough.

pc.expect: The foot catches on the rug and the body pitches forward, and the plates go with it.
pc.fail: The person trips on bare floor away from the rug; or the plates fly before the trip; or they fly backward.

pc.expect: The plates are thrown forward, the way the person was going.
pc.fail: They go backward; or straight up; or scatter from a point on the floor before landing.

pc.expect: The person keeps their limbs and shape, and the plates keep their number until they break.
pc.fail: A limb detaches; or plates multiply in the air; or the person passes through the floor.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The plates' pattern, the rug and the room stay the same.
pc.fail: The plates change pattern; or the rug changes colour; or the room rearranges.

note: The person is kept because their stumble is what launches the plates. Their balance and how they fall are not judged.
